title: Kenafric KPI definition submission (v1.0)
description: The body of a POST to WF-18b (kenafric-wf18b): a line manager's probation KPI set for one employee. Four keys and nothing else — additionalProperties is false, so a stray key is rejected rather than ignored. Keyed by MEANING rather than by ClickUp field id, unlike the feedback layer: there the question set is fixed and the ids are the stable contract, here the rows vary and the fields are few, so WF-18b resolves eight ids once. No ClickUp field id, option UUID or list id appears in this payload. Validated against real payloads by src/kpi/payload.test.ts with Ajv — against this file, not against the app's opinion of it.

t.description: The signed token from the link, passed through verbatim. base64url payload, '.', base64url HMAC-SHA256. The app never decodes it: a claim read from an unverified token is a claim the holder could have rewritten. n8n verifies it against LINK_SECRET — the same secret as WF-11d/11e and WF-21..25, never a second one. It is also the idempotency key: WF-18b stores it as KPI Set Token and refuses one already on the list.

formType.description: Echoed back from what the context endpoint said, so WF-18b can branch without decoding its own token twice. Never a value the browser chose.

submittedAt.description: ISO 8601 with the local UTC offset, never Z. Every one of these is submitted in Nairobi, and a 09:00 EAT submission filed as 06:00 UTC reads as a manager answering before the email went out.

kpis.description: Three to five KPIs, in the order the manager entered them. The form will not submit unless the weights total exactly 100; WF-18b's own check is ADVISORY and never blocking, because refusing a hand-made set at 99 would discard a manager's real work over a bookkeeping rule.

keyResultArea.description: The area of the business this KPI sits in. Free text, because the ClickUp field is short_text — K-2 is open, and a fixed list would be the better answer for cross-department reporting.

kpi.description: The KPI statement. Becomes the ClickUp task name, which caps at 100 characters — a KPI that arrives truncated is a KPI nobody agreed to.

measurementType.description: The ClickUp Measurement Type option NAME, never its UUID. It decides which scoring path the final review takes: actual over target, or rating over five.

howMeasured.description: The report, register or system the figure is read from, and how often. This is what makes an actual figure mean anything three months later.

targetFigure.description: Quantitative rows only, and ABSENT on a qualitative one — not null, not 0. Never zero: the score is a division by it, and the form refuses a zero target outright.

unitOfMeasure.description: Quantitative rows only, and absent on a qualitative one. What the figure is counted in — KES, %, units, days, hours, count.

target.description: The target as a sentence. This is what the review is actually read against, and what the employee sees.

weight.description: Percentage of the review this KPI carries. No single KPI above 60 — one KPI carrying the whole review is not a review — and none below 5, which is a row that exists only to make the arithmetic work.

allOf.description: A quantitative KPI cannot be scored without a target figure and a unit.
A qualitative KPI has no figure to hit, so sending an empty one would write two blank values to ClickUp — and 'does not apply' reports differently from 'left blank'.
